value.rationale: The tradeoff between quadratic within-habitat crowding and saturating predation creates a natural nonconcave prey-allocation problem. Its exact global solution predicts, for arbitrary n, a complete no-skipping sequence of occupied-habitat transitions at measurable model thresholds; this is stronger than a trivial Jensen inequality or a single two-patch numerical case. It does not claim field behavior or long-term optimal control.
